security_spec.violation_condition: When CHERI is enabled, QEMU TCG translates a vector load/store instruction with base register x0 as a valid memory access (e.g., treating base=0 as a null-derived capability covering all memory) instead of raising an illegal instruction exception as required by the 'reserved' encoding rule
security_spec.summary: Under CHERI, vector memory access instructions with base register x0 are reserved encodings; failing to trap them in QEMU TCG allows guests to bypass capability bounds enforcement via XLEN-wide indexed offsets that effectively access arbitrary physical memory

findings.finding: Unit-stride vector load/store uses get_gpr(s, rs1, EXT_NONE) to obtain the base address without any check for rs1==x0. Under CHERI, an instruction with x0 as base must be reserved (raise illegal instruction), but this code treats base=0 as a valid address. No CHERI capability infrastructure exists in this codebase yet, so the risk is latent until CHERI support is added.

spec_citations.excerpt: Additionally, the standard CHERI rule that all loads and stores where the base register is x0 are reserved applies to all vector memory access instructions.

findings.finding: Stride vector load/store uses get_gpr(s, rs1, EXT_NONE) at line 891 to obtain the base address. No check for rs1==x0. Under CHERI, x0-based vector loads/stores are reserved encodings and must raise illegal instruction exception.

spec_citations.excerpt: Additionally, the standard CHERI rule that all loads and stores where the base register is x0 are reserved applies to all vector memory access instructions.

findings.finding: Indexed vector load/store uses get_gpr(s, rs1, EXT_NONE) at line 993 to obtain the base address. The CHERI spec explicitly notes that 'indexed loads with the base register set to the value zero and XLEN-wide offsets does not work well with CHERI' and x0 base must be reserved.

spec_citations.excerpt: Additionally, the standard CHERI rule that all loads and stores where the base register is x0 are reserved applies to all vector memory access instructions. NOTE: The approach of using indexed loads with the base register set to the value zero and XLEN-wide offsets does not work well with CHERI as the authorizing capability must cover all of memory. If the authorizing capability is specified as x0 then the instruction encoding is reserved.

findings.finding: Fault-only-first vector load uses get_gpr(s, rs1, EXT_NONE) at line 1129. No x0 base check. Under CHERI, fault-only-first loads with x0 base must also be reserved per the general vector memory access rule.

spec_citations.excerpt: Under CHERI, vector loads and stores follow the standard rules for active elements: ... CHERI exceptions are only raised on fault-only-first loads if element 0 is both active and fails any exception checks. Additionally, the standard CHERI rule that all loads and stores where the base register is x0 are reserved applies to all vector memory access instructions.

findings.finding: Whole-register vector load/store has two paths: (1) inline TCG generation using get_address(s, rs1, i) in a loop (line 1207) and (2) helper function path using get_gpr(s, rs1, EXT_NONE) (line 1230). Neither path checks for xs1==x0. Under CHERI, x0-base whole-register loads/stores are reserved.

spec_citations.excerpt: Additionally, the standard CHERI rule that all loads and stores where the base register is x0 are reserved applies to all vector memory access instructions.
